name_reason: Name is correct and convention-compliant. Prefix data_fd2_battle_ marks a battle-core table/state global (battle convention). Descriptor summon_anim_variant_b_6slot identifies the owning state machine: the variant-B 6-slot summon-spell animation (fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_b_6slot), the only accessor. The 'b' is a variant label distinguishing the two summon animations A/B (variant-A is the sibling at 0x269D3), not an address residue. The '6slot' is a real array dimension (6 elements), confirmed by byte[6] and the 6-iteration access loop; a meaningful count, not address residue. jitter_byte_array reflects content (per-slot vertical jitter), element width (byte) and data type (array). No hex address residue anywhere in the name (the only hex tokens are in the comment as @-address annotations).
purpose: Per-slot vertical jitter (6 slots, one byte each) for the variant-B 6-slot summon-spell animation state machine; an additive offset folded into each slot's sprite frame index when blitting that slot's sprite.
logic_summary: Zero-bss runtime state written and read exclusively by fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_b_6slot (0x26BFD..0x26E34). INIT state (state_code==0) seeds each of the 6 slots with (rng % 2) * 6 = 0 or 6 (store @ 0x26C97). The TICK frame-7 wrap/color-rotation path (frame counter hits 7 with terminate_flag==0) re-rolls the slot with the same (rng % 2) * 6 (store @ 0x26D9D). In every TICK frame (state 2/5/8) the value is read (@ 0x26DE4) and added to the slot's frame counter to form the sprite frame index passed to fd2_blit_indexed_sprite. (Variant-A at 0x269D3 uses 0 or 7 instead of 0 or 6.) Sibling state arrays for the same machine: frame_counter_array (0x5401C, int[6]), color_idx_array (0x54034, int[6]); rotation source is data_fd2_battle_summon_anim_variant_b_color_rotation_counter (0x54052, mod-10 byte).
element_semantics: Each uint8 element is the vertical jitter for one of the 6 animation slots: always 0 or 6 (rng % 2 scaled by 6). Accessed as BYTE (stride 1): writes via 'MOV byte ptr [idx + 0x5404C],DL' (0x26C97 INIT, 0x26D9D re-roll); read zero-extended via 'MOVZX EDX, byte ptr [idx + 0x5404C]' (0x26DE4), confirming unsigned 8-bit elements. Index always 0..5 (6-iteration loop, var_14<6).

All match the decompiled accessor, disassembly, and xrefs exactly, so the comment was kept unchanged.
